title: 6-round AES-256: reported whole-key partial sums, five-byte filter

display.name: Partial sums, five-byte filter, full-key headline

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 6-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-6r-integral-fklssww2001-partial-sums; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Six chosen-plaintext structures, each varying the four bytes feeding one first-round column over all 2^32 possibilities and fixing the other bytes.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.reported: about 2^52 S-box applications, approximately 2^44 trial encryptions
time.note: The six-structure total is about 2^52 S-box applications. Division by the authors' rough 2^8 S-box applications per trial encryption gives 2^44; this is their cost model, not a modern calibrated AES implementation. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: Section 2.3 uses about six structures to identify the five subkey bytes. This is the full filtering data, not six plaintexts. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.reported: 2^24-bit first counter array; input list and other working storage separately required
memory.note: Section 2.3 explicitly prices the first partial-sum counter array at 2^24 bits and starts from a list of 2^32 ciphertexts. The array alone is not asserted to be whole-attack peak memory.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: No numerical key_recovery success is stated at this exact structure budget. The direct and partial-sums implementations preserve the same aggregate XOR. The 255/256 wrong-key rejection in Section2.1 is for one 256-text Lambda set in the older algorithm; it is not assigned to the improved 2^32-text aggregate or exponentiated over this endpoint. About six structures are said to identify the five-byte hypothesis, without an explicit joint probability or full-key completion distribution. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF3–6 Sections2.3–2.4: a correctly hypothesized targeted byte has zero XOR over the complete 2^32-text structure, since it partitions into balanced 256-text sets. Partial sums compute the same XOR exactly; the identity does not imply unique recovery.
